stem: What term refers to the probability of having a condition when the test result is positive?
explanation: Positive predictive value is the probability that a person truly has the condition given that the test result is positive. Sensitivity and specificity describe test performance in people with and without disease, respectively, while pre-test probability is the estimated chance of disease before testing. Negative predictive value is the probability of not having the condition when the test is negative.

optionExplanations.A: Sensitivity is the proportion of people with the condition who test positive
optionExplanations.B: Specificity is the proportion of people without the condition who test negative
optionExplanations.C: Pre-test probability is the estimated likelihood of disease before the test is performed
optionExplanations.D: Negative predictive value is the probability of not having the condition when the test is negative
optionExplanations.E: Positive predictive value is the probability of having the condition when the test is positive
